You are helping a user write SQL queries to a database. If something is not clear, you can ask the user to clarify what they need. The schema for the database being accessed is the following:
        
CREATE TABLE Addresses (
    address_id INTEGER   PRIMARY KEY,
    line_1 VARCHAR(255),
    line_2 VARCHAR(255),
    line_3 VARCHAR(255),
    city VARCHAR(255),
    zip_postcode VARCHAR(20),
    state_province_county VARCHAR(255),
    country VARCHAR(255),
    other_address_details VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE Courses (
    course_id INTEGER   PRIMARY KEY,
    course_name VARCHAR(255),
    course_description VARCHAR(255),
    other_details VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE Departments (
    department_id INTEGER   PRIMARY KEY,
    department_name VARCHAR(255),
    department_description VARCHAR(255),
    other_details VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE Degree_Programs (
    degree_program_id INTEGER   PRIMARY KEY,
    department_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    degree_summary_name VARCHAR(255),
    degree_summary_description VARCHAR(255),
    other_details VARCHAR(255),
    FOREIGN KEY (department_id) REFERENCES Departments(department_id)
);

CREATE TABLE Sections (
    section_id INTEGER   PRIMARY KEY,
    course_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    section_name VARCHAR(255),
    section_description VARCHAR(255),
    other_details VARCHAR(255),
    FOREIGN KEY (course_id) REFERENCES Courses(course_id)
);

CREATE TABLE Semesters (
    semester_id INTEGER   PRIMARY KEY,
    semester_name VARCHAR(255),
    semester_description VARCHAR(255),
    other_details VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE Students (
    student_id INTEGER   PRIMARY KEY,
    current_address_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    permanent_address_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    first_name VARCHAR(80),
    middle_name VARCHAR(40),
    last_name VARCHAR(40),
    cell_mobile_number VARCHAR(40),
    email_address VARCHAR(40),
    ssn VARCHAR(40),
    date_first_registered DATETIME,
    date_left DATETIME,
    other_student_details VARCHAR(255),
    FOREIGN KEY (permanent_address_id) REFERENCES Addresses(address_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (current_address_id) REFERENCES Addresses(address_id)
);

CREATE TABLE Student_Enrolment (
    student_enrolment_id INTEGER   PRIMARY KEY,
    degree_program_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    semester_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    student_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    other_details VARCHAR(255),
    FOREIGN KEY (student_id) REFERENCES Students(student_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (semester_id) REFERENCES Semesters(semester_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (degree_program_id) REFERENCES Degree_Programs(degree_program_id)
);

CREATE TABLE Student_Enrolment_Courses (
    student_course_id INTEGER   PRIMARY KEY,
    course_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    student_enrolment_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    FOREIGN KEY (student_enrolment_id) REFERENCES Student_Enrolment(student_enrolment_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (course_id) REFERENCES Courses(course_id)
);

CREATE TABLE Transcripts (
    transcript_id INTEGER   PRIMARY KEY,
    transcript_date DATETIME,
    other_details VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE Transcript_Contents (
    student_course_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    transcript_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    FOREIGN KEY (transcript_id) REFERENCES Transcripts(transcript_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (student_course_id) REFERENCES Student_Enrolment_Courses(student_course_id)
);

What transcript info are you trying to gather (and at what “level”)?

Here are the most common transcript-focused queries you can use with your schema—pick one and tell me any filters (student, semester, date range, degree program, etc.) and I’ll tailor it.

## 1) List all transcripts (header info)
```sql
SELECT
  t.transcript_id,
  t.transcript_date,
  t.other_details
FROM Transcripts t
ORDER BY t.transcript_date DESC, t.transcript_id DESC;
```

## 2) Transcript contents (which student-course records are on each transcript)
```sql
SELECT
  t.transcript_id,
  t.transcript_date,
  tc.student_course_id
FROM Transcripts t
JOIN Transcript_Contents tc
  ON tc.transcript_id = t.transcript_id
ORDER BY t.transcript_id, tc.student_course_id;
```

## 3) Full transcript “details” (transcript → courses → student/semester/degree)
This is usually what people mean by “transcript info” given your schema.
```sql
SELECT
  t.transcript_id,
  t.transcript_date,

  s.student_id,
  s.first_name,
  s.last_name,

  sem.semester_id,
  sem.semester_name,

  dp.degree_program_id,
  dp.degree_summary_name,
  d.department_name,

  c.course_id,
  c.course_name,

  sec.section_id,
  sec.section_name
FROM Transcripts t
JOIN Transcript_Contents tc
  ON tc.transcript_id = t.transcript_id
JOIN Student_Enrolment_Courses secourse
  ON secourse.student_course_id = tc.student_course_id
JOIN Courses c
  ON c.course_id = secourse.course_id
JOIN Student_Enrolment se
  ON se.student_enrolment_id = secourse.student_enrolment_id
JOIN Students s
  ON s.student_id = se.student_id
JOIN Semesters sem
  ON sem.semester_id = se.semester_id
JOIN Degree_Programs dp
  ON dp.degree_program_id = se.degree_program_id
JOIN Departments d
  ON d.department_id = dp.department_id
LEFT JOIN Sections sec
  ON sec.course_id = c.course_id
ORDER BY
  t.transcript_id, s.student_id, sem.semester_id, c.course_name;
```

## 4) Get transcript for one student (parameterized)
```sql
SELECT
  t.transcript_id,
  t.transcript_date,
  c.course_id,
  c.course_name,
  sem.semester_name,
  dp.degree_summary_name
FROM Transcripts t
JOIN Transcript_Contents tc ON tc.transcript_id = t.transcript_id
JOIN Student_Enrolment_Courses secourse ON secourse.student_course_id = tc.student_course_id
JOIN Courses c ON c.course_id = secourse.course_id
JOIN Student_Enrolment se ON se.student_enrolment_id = secourse.student_enrolment_id
JOIN Semesters sem ON sem.semester_id = se.semester_id
JOIN Degree_Programs dp ON dp.degree_program_id = se.degree_program_id
WHERE se.student_id = :student_id
ORDER BY t.transcript_date DESC, sem.semester_name, c.course_name;
```

### Clarifying questions
1) Do you want transcripts **per student**, **per transcript_id**, or **per semester**?  
2) Should the output include **address/contact info** from `Students`/`Addresses`?  
3) Do you track **grades/credits** somewhere else? (Not present in this schema.)
also need transcript dates and IDs

To include **transcript IDs and transcript dates**, join `Transcripts` to `Transcript_Contents` and then out to the student/course context.

### Transcript IDs + dates (with student and course info)
```sql
SELECT
  t.transcript_id,
  t.transcript_date,
  s.student_id,
  s.first_name,
  s.last_name,
  c.course_id,
  c.course_name
FROM Transcripts t
JOIN Transcript_Contents tc
  ON tc.transcript_id = t.transcript_id
JOIN Student_Enrolment_Courses sec
  ON sec.student_course_id = tc.student_course_id
JOIN Student_Enrolment se
  ON se.student_enrolment_id = sec.student_enrolment_id
JOIN Students s
  ON s.student_id = se.student_id
JOIN Courses c
  ON c.course_id = sec.course_id
ORDER BY t.transcript_date DESC, t.transcript_id, s.student_id, c.course_name;
```

### If you only want the list of transcript IDs + dates
```sql
SELECT transcript_id, transcript_date
FROM Transcripts
ORDER BY transcript_date DESC, transcript_id DESC;
```

If you tell me whether you want it **for a specific student** (and their `student_id`), I can add the `WHERE` clause.
I also need transcripts that have at least 2 course results.

```sql
SELECT
  t.transcript_id,
  t.transcript_date,
  COUNT(tc.student_course_id) AS course_results_count
FROM Transcripts t
JOIN Transcript_Contents tc
  ON tc.transcript_id = t.transcript_id
GROUP BY
  t.transcript_id,
  t.transcript_date
HAVING COUNT(tc.student_course_id) >= 2
ORDER BY t.transcript_date DESC, t.transcript_id DESC;
```

If you want “course results” to mean **distinct courses** (in case the same course can appear multiple times), say so and I’ll switch the count to `COUNT(DISTINCT ...)`.
I need to include the ids of each transcript too.

The query already includes the transcript IDs (`t.transcript_id`). If you meant you want the **IDs of the student_course results on each transcript** as well, use this:

```sql
SELECT
  t.transcript_id,
  t.transcript_date,
  tc.student_course_id
FROM Transcripts t
JOIN Transcript_Contents tc
  ON tc.transcript_id = t.transcript_id
WHERE tc.transcript_id IN (
  SELECT transcript_id
  FROM Transcript_Contents
  GROUP BY transcript_id
  HAVING COUNT(student_course_id) >= 2
)
ORDER BY t.transcript_date DESC, t.transcript_id DESC, tc.student_course_id;
```

If you tell me your SQL dialect (SQLite/Postgres/MySQL/SQL Server), I can also return the `student_course_id` values aggregated into one row per transcript.
